cards.title: Nuclear pasta inside neutron stars is 10 billion times stronger than steel
cards.body: Deep inside the crust of a dead neutron star, immense pressure forces protons and neutrons into exotic shapes resembling gnocchi, spaghetti, and lasagna. Known to astrophysicists as nuclear pasta, computer simulations show that breaking this dense cosmic matter requires ten billion times the force needed to shatter steel, making it by far the strongest material known to exist anywhere in the cosmos.

sources.title: Neutron star 'pasta' is the strongest material in the universe
Nuclear Pasta Hardest Substance in Universe

cards.title: The Sun's core spins nearly four times faster than its outer surface
cards.body: While astronomers have long known that the Sun's visible surface spins once every 25 to 35 days, measurements of acoustic and gravitational waves by the SOHO spacecraft revealed a hidden interior rhythm. The Sun's scorching core actually spins nearly four times faster than its outer layers, completing a full rotation once every week. Scientists believe this rapid spin is a lingering remnant from the cloud that birthed the solar system.

sources.title: Sun's core rotates four times faster than its surface

cards.title: Scientists used Saturn's rings as a seismograph to clock its day
cards.body: Because Saturn is a swirling ball of gas with no solid landmarks and a magnetic field eerily aligned with its spin, astronomers could not determine its exact rotational period for decades. In 2019, scientists finally cracked the mystery using Cassini data. As Saturn rotates, internal vibrations ripple through its gravitational field, creating spiral wave patterns in its icy rings. Analyzing these wave seismographs clocked Saturn's true day at 10 hours, 33 minutes, and 38 seconds.

sources.title: Cassini Data Solves Saturn's Rotation Puzzle

cards.title: The high clouds of Uranus smell like rotten eggs
cards.body: For decades, astronomers debated whether the high clouds shrouding ice giant Uranus were composed primarily of ammonia ice or hydrogen sulfide. In 2018, sensitive infrared spectrometers on the Gemini North telescope detected the unmistakable spectral signature of hydrogen sulfide gas in Uranus's cloud tops. The noxious compound, notorious on Earth for giving rotten eggs their pungent stench, blankets the planet in a frigid, foul-smelling layer high above its interior.

sources.title: Gemini Spacecraft Confirms Hydrogen Sulfide in Clouds of Uranus

cards.title: A solitary dust devil on Mars once towered 20 kilometers high
cards.body: Mars is famous for intense swirling vortices of dust, but in 2012, NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter captured something extraordinary: a dust devil towering 20 kilometers into the Martian sky. Despite rising higher than Mount Everest, the column was only about 70 meters wide at its base. Mars's thin atmosphere and massive thermal contrasts allow these delicate, towering whirlwinds to stretch into the stratosphere, lofting reddish dust across the planet.

quizzes.question: What makes 'nuclear pasta' inside neutron stars extraordinary to physicists?
options: It is 10 billion times stronger than steel
It boils into a gas at room temperature
It generates an electric current with zero resistance
It dissolves instantly in strong magnetic fields
quizzes.explanation: Simulations show that deforming or breaking nuclear pasta requires roughly 10 billion times the force needed to break steel.

quizzes.question: How does the rotation speed of the Sun's core compare to its surface?
options: It rotates nearly four times faster than the surface
It spins backward relative to the surface
It does not spin at all and remains locked in place
It rotates at roughly half the speed of the surface
quizzes.explanation: SOHO observations revealed that the solar core completes a rotation about once every week, nearly four times faster than the surface.

quizzes.question: How did astronomers finally determine the exact length of a day on Saturn?
options: By tracking spiral wave vibrations in its rings
By landing a robotic seismometer on its rocky core
By measuring the orbit of its innermost moon
By monitoring a fixed dark cloud feature at its equator
quizzes.explanation: Vibrations inside Saturn distort its gravity field and produce spiral waves in its rings, acting as a seismograph that clocked its rotation.

quizzes.question: What compound was detected in Uranus's upper clouds that produces the stench of rotten eggs?
options: Hydrogen sulfide
Ammonia
Sulfur dioxide
Carbon monoxide
quizzes.explanation: Spectroscopic measurements by the Gemini telescope confirmed that Uranus's cloud tops are rich in hydrogen sulfide gas.

quizzes.question: What altitude did a record-breaking Martian dust devil reach in 2012?
options: 20 kilometers (12 miles)
2 kilometers (1.2 miles)
80 kilometers (50 miles)
500 meters (1,640 feet)
quizzes.explanation: NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter imaged an active dust devil whose towering plume reached 20 kilometers high.

guesses.prompt: By what factor does the Sun's deep core rotate faster than its visible surface?
guesses.explanation: The Sun's core completes a rotation once a week, nearly four times faster than its surface, which takes about 25 to 35 days.

guesses.prompt: In 2012, a NASA orbiter photographed a towering dust devil on Mars. How high did its plume reach in kilometers?
guesses.explanation: The Martian whirlwind rose 20 kilometers (12 miles) high—more than twice the height of Mount Everest—despite being only 70 meters wide at the ground.

misconceptions.claim: The Sun rotates as a single rigid sphere from its core to its surface.
misconceptions.explanation: The Sun undergoes differential rotation: its surface rotates at different speeds depending on latitude, while its core spins four times faster than the surface.

misconceptions.claim: Uranus's cloud tops are mainly composed of ammonia ice, just like Jupiter and Saturn.
misconceptions.explanation: Unlike Jupiter and Saturn, where ammonia dominates the cloud deck, spectroscopic data confirmed Uranus's upper clouds are composed of hydrogen sulfide.

misconceptions.claim: A single dust devil on Mars can tower higher than Mount Everest.
misconceptions.explanation: Because of low gravity and strong temperature gradients, Martian dust devils can reach heights of 20 kilometers, dwarfing Earth's highest peaks.
